source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

33001.t:
Belknap County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by much less than in 2024. Sununu leads Pappas 15,867 to 14,884, a 3-point margin, down from Trump's 13-point win over Harris. That is a 10-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical New Hampshire county's 12 and the typical county nationally at 14. It ranks 7th of the state's 10 counties. Coos, which voted much like Belknap in 2024, moved 12 points and also stayed Republican.

Only 73% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 31,374 votes so far equal 77% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

33003.t:
Carroll County, which Trump carried by 2 points in 2024, voted for Democrat Pappas over Republican Sununu by 6 points in the U.S. Senate race, 14,680 to 13,015, with all of the expected vote counted. That 8-point move toward the Democrats flipped the county, one of three in New Hampshire to go from Trump to the Democrat. It was still the smallest shift among the state's 10 counties, all of which moved left, typically by 12 points. Comparable counties moved further: Rockingham by 10, Sullivan by 11 and Merrimack by 13.

Turnout was 28,140, or 82% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

33007.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Coos County stayed Republican, but barely: Sununu leads Pappas 6,398 to 6,219, a margin of about 1 point, after Trump carried it by 14 in 2024. That is a 12-point move toward the Democrats, close to the state's 11-point shift and the typical New Hampshire county's 12. Coos ranks fifth of 10 counties by move and last by votes cast. Comparable counties moved by different amounts: Belknap by 10 points, Sullivan by 11 and Carroll by 8.

Only 12,952 votes have been counted, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 92% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

33009.t:
Grafton County moved toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, but by less than most of New Hampshire. Kamala Harris carried it by 20 points in 2024; Chris Pappas leads John Sununu here by 30, 28,161 votes to 15,153. That shift of about 10 points ranks eighth of the state's 10 counties, all of which moved left, typically by 12. Similar counties moved further: Strafford by 15, Merrimack by 13 and Cheshire by 12. Statewide, Pappas won by 14.

About 44,129 votes have been cast, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

33019.t:
Sullivan County flipped. Trump carried it by less than a point in 2024, and in the U.S. Senate race Pappas led Sununu here by 10 points, 10,426 votes to 8,408, a move of 11 points toward the Democrats. That matches the statewide swing of 11 points and sits just below the typical New Hampshire county's 12. All 10 counties in the state moved left, and this was one of three to go from a Trump win to a Democratic win. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points.

Only 85% of the expected vote is counted, so the numbers may still move. The 19,363 votes so far equal 77% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

33011.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Pappas and Sununu, Hillsborough County swung 13 points toward the Democrats, from a 3-point Harris edge in 2024 to a 16-point Pappas lead: 120,000 votes to 86,224. That is slightly more than the state's 11-point shift and the second-largest move among New Hampshire's 10 counties, all of which moved left. Hillsborough cast the most votes in the state. Neighboring Rockingham moved 10 points and Merrimack 13.

Only about 84% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 210,340 votes so far equal 90% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

33013.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Merrimack County voted for Democrat Pappas over Republican Sununu by 18 points, 41,820 to 29,012. That is 13 points more Democratic than its 5-point margin for Harris in 2024, slightly more than the typical New Hampshire county's 12-point shift, putting it third of 10 in the state. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Hillsborough by 13 points, Cheshire by 12.

Only 75% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 72,395 votes so far equal 78% of the 2024 total. With turnout down that much, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

33015.t:
Rockingham County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, backing Democrat Pappas over Republican Sununu by 7 points, 83,554 to 72,412, after favoring Trump by 2 in 2024. That 10-point swing toward the Democrats trails the statewide move of 11 and the typical New Hampshire county's 12, ranking ninth of ten. Nearby Hillsborough moved 13 points. Nationally, the typical county moved 14.

About 158,404 votes have been counted, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With just 91% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

33017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Strafford County voted for Pappas over Sununu by 27 points, 53,638 to 30,347, up from Harris's 12-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 15-point shift toward the Democrats is the largest of New Hampshire's 10 counties, all of which moved left, against a typical county move of 12 points. It also outpaced similar counties such as Cheshire and Merrimack, which each moved 12 points.

Turnout rose. The 85,442 votes counted so far are 112% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who newly voted. With only 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

33005.t:
Cheshire County voted for Pappas over Sununu in the U.S. Senate race by 22 points, 20,620 to 12,949, after backing Harris over Trump by 10 points in 2024. That is a move of 12 points toward the Democrats, slightly more than the state's 11-point swing and close to the typical New Hampshire county's, ranking fourth of 10. Among similar counties, Strafford moved 15 points, Merrimack 13 and Grafton 10.

About 34,448 votes have been counted, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With only 81% of the expected vote in, these numbers may still move.
